newsitem.title: USA: KeyCorp cuts jobs in national restructuring.
newsitem.headline: KeyCorp cuts jobs in national restructuring.

text.p: KeyCorp said Monday that it is forming a single nationwide bank from its 12-bank network in a restructuring that should cut 2,700 jobs.

KeyCorp said the job cuts represent about 10 percent of its employment base. The company said it plans to sell slightly more than 140 of its branch offices, known as KeyCenters, in primarily rural areas.
KeyCorp said the restructuring will result in a fourth quarter charge of $100 million, but provide about $110 million in annualized earnings benefits by the end of 1997.

"These are bold steps that will complete the process we launched 18 months ago to transform Key into a nationwide financial services provider," KeyCorp Chief Executive Robert Gillespie said in a release.
The company said transformation from a multi-state office network will prepare the franchise for full interstate banking in 1997. It said about 1,000 KeyCenters will remain after the changes.
The job cuts will be throughout the company at all job levels, KeyCorp said.
The fourth quarter charges will include $20 million for branch consolidation, $52 million in job-cutting costs and $28 million for technology write-offs, the company said.

It said the restructuring and expense reduction programs outlined earlier this year should help it achieve a previously-announced efficiency ratio target of 55 percent by the end of 1997, with further improvement thereafter.
